title: A Frontend trader who spots a wrong saved address on a party picker can only read it; Design release 1 links every row to the saved record, where it can be edited or deleted before the trader is returned to the picker

finding.frontend: On a Frontend party picker each row's "View details" is a disclosure that opens in place (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:28-41), revealing the saved record as a plain list built from name, address lines, country, telephone number and email address (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/view-model/address-lines.js:15-22). The captured place-of-origin picker carries five of them, and the first opens to seven lines for Astra Rosales ending "01632 960000" and "astra-rosales@example.com". The row offers nothing else: no Edit, no Delete, no link out. So a trader who sees that a saved consignor has moved, that a postcode is wrong, or that the same farm is in the book twice, has no way to correct or remove it anywhere in this service, and the only thing they can do is pick the wrong record or abandon the section. Searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "edit address", "change this address", "edit this address" and "delete address" returns nothing. This is deliberate in the code: the address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and says "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The transporter list is the same shape, its rows leading nowhere either.
finding.prototype: In Design release 1 the same "View details" is a link out of the row to the saved address's own page, carrying the page the trader came from in a return parameter, so a row on the place-of-origin picker points at /address-book/<id>?return=%2Fplace-of-origin (app/views/consignment-address-select.html:152, with the href built at app/routes.js:3562). That page is dr1-address-book-view: the record's name as the heading, a summary list of eight facts, and then an "Edit" button beside a red "Delete" button. Edit opens dr1-address-book-edit, headed "Edit address and contact details", with all nine address and contact fields prefilled and already open, the address search suppressed, and "Save changes" beside "Cancel"; the return parameter is carried into the form action, so saving or cancelling puts the trader back on the picker they left rather than stranding them in the address book, and the delete honours the same parameter. Design release 1's transporter list links its rows to the same record page. So in Design release 1 a wrong saved address is fixed where it is noticed, and the notification is never abandoned.
finding.difference: Give every picker row a route to the saved record and a way back to the page the trader left. This is the maintenance half of the route the add finding covers, and it turns on the same choice of destination: either an address record page inside this frontend, which means giving its address-book service the update and delete it deliberately does not have (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19), or a link into the Import Notification Service front door's existing address-book record and edit pages, which needs a return URL so the trader comes back to the picker. The address-book API already serves update and delete, so nothing has to land first either way and the band is frontend-work. Raise it separately from the add route because it is a different control, a different user need -- correcting or removing a record rather than creating one -- and because it was until now carried by nobody: the addresses slice recorded both "View details" behaviours and passed the question to address-book--saved-address-book-pages-absent, and the transport slice left Design release 1's transporter "View details" link out for the same reason, but neither that finding nor the add-route finding asks for the route. Whether the in-place disclosure survives alongside the link is a design call for whoever does the work; Design release 1 shows only the link. The named control, "View details", occurs five times on the Frontend picker and nine times on the Design release 1 one, so both cards will be refused a crop and fall back to the whole page with the reason printed. That is the right picture here: the finding is about what a row leads to, not about one row.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any control on a Frontend party picker, transporter list or contact-address page that leads to changing or removing a saved address-book record.
finding.verification: Written and checked by me, the coverage auditor for the address-book slice, so a reader should know this finding had no independent verifier -- I am both its author and its only check. Ran the falsifier: grepped all 67 captured Frontend DOM files for "edit address", "change this address", "edit this address" and "delete address" and got nothing, then read fe-address-picker-place-of-origin.html around each of its five "View details" occurrences -- every one is a govuk-details summary whose disclosed content is a govuk-list of address lines, the phone number and the email, with no anchor and no button in the cell. Read the frontend citations at the lines given: _address-picker.njk:28-41 is the detailsCell, address-lines.js:15-22 is detailLines, and services/address-book/index.js:17-19 carries the read-only comment verbatim. On the Design release 1 side, counted nine "View details" occurrences in dr1-consignment-address-select.html and confirmed each is an anchor to /address-book/<id>?return=%2Fplace-of-origin; checked both citations are root views or root routes -- app/views/consignment-address-select.html:152 renders address.viewHref and app/routes.js:3562 builds it with the return path. Opened dr1-address-book-view.png and dr1-address-book-edit.png: the view page shows the eight summary rows with Edit and a red Delete beneath, and the edit page shows all nine fields prefilled with "Save changes" and "Cancel". Read app/routes.js:7858-7888 to confirm the edit page reuses the address-book-lookup view with isEditMode, the heading "Edit address and contact details" and a form action carrying the return query, and app/routes.js:9946-9998 to confirm both edit and delete redirect to that return path. Checked this is not a fixture difference under the contract's test: swapping either side's stub for real data leaves it exactly where it is, because the difference is the existence of a route out of the row. Checked it does not duplicate address-book--no-route-to-add-an-address-from-a-picker, which is about the "Add a new address" button and creating a record, or addresses--picker-pages-results-and-searches-on-the-server, whose correction states the two "View details" behaviours and explicitly hands the question to this slice without raising it.

relatedTo.why: The same row needs two routes out -- one to create a record and one to correct the one it is showing -- and both land on the same choice of destination, so they are built together.
Where the row's link goes is the scope question that finding states; this one is the part of it that bites a trader inside the notification journey today, whichever way the scope question is settled.
